subject: Trump said he'd never touch Social Security
preheader: His own actuary says the bill cost it $169 billion. Plus: Buffett's will, and the drug-plan subsidy that just died.
greeting: Good morning. Promises are easy to make and hard to audit. Today's issue checks three of them against the numbers: a president's pledge on Social Security, a billionaire's instructions for his own family, and a Medicare subsidy that was always going to expire, whatever you were told.
today: Trump promised not to touch Social Security, and the agency's own actuary says his bill cost it $169 billion
Warren Buffett's will puts 90% of his wife's inheritance in one fund. Here's what a retiree should copy, and change
The $9.8 billion subsidy holding down drug-plan premiums is gone, and three in four people in those plans will pay more

headline.title: Social Security's retirement fund now runs short in late 2032
headline.stat_label: of scheduled benefits payable once the trust fund is depleted, under current law
headline.text: The 2026 Trustees Report moved the depletion date up one quarter, to the fourth quarter of 2032. On an average $2,000 check, the automatic cut would be about $440 a month, and the trustees point at two policy shifts for the change.

stories.why: The Social Security Administration's chief actuary put the cost of the 2025 tax law at $168.6 billion over ten years and said it alone moved the retirement fund's depletion date from early 2033 to late 2032. A 22% automatic cut would land on current retirees, not just future ones.

The instruction is 90% in a low-cost S&P 500 index fund and 10% in short-term Treasuries, and nothing else. The simplicity is worth copying. The 90/10 ratio is where a retiree who is drawing on savings every month should differ.

Medicare's own projection is that about 75% of stand-alone drug-plan enrollees will see a premium increase in 2027, most of them in the $11 to $20 a month range. The Annual Notice of Change arriving by September 30 is where you'll find out.

quiz.q: Early estimates put the 2027 Social Security cost-of-living adjustment at roughly what percentage?
quiz.explain: The Senior Citizens League's August estimate is about 3.6%, which would be the largest COLA since 2023. This year's was 2.8%. The official number arrives with the September inflation report in mid-October, and most of it goes out on the January payment, minus whatever Medicare Part B adds.
